visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A young woman with medium-length brown hair, wearing a black T-shirt and blue jeans, stands in a room with a light gray wall. She looks directly at the camera, speaking and gesturing with her hands. A small black rectangular object is held in her right hand near her chest. The lighting is warm and bright, coming from the side. (2) The scene shifts to a slightly closer shot as she closes her eyes and uses her index finger to point toward her nose. She smiles slightly as she touches her nose accurately. Large white and yellow subtitles appear at the bottom of the frame. (3) A series of short cuts show different individuals participating in the test. A woman in a yellow shirt with glasses closes her eyes and points to her nose. Then, a split-screen shows a young woman and a man both performing the same action. They are in similar indoor settings with warm lighting. (4) The video cuts to two more young men in a split-screen, both with their eyes closed, attempting to touch their noses. One man smiles as he succeeds, while the other looks focused. Captions with green and white text overlay their faces. (5) The main woman returns to the full frame, standing in the same position. She gestures expansively with her hands as she explains the results of the coordination test. She appears energetic and engaging. (6) The woman in the yellow shirt is shown again, now standing in a dimly lit area of the room. She begins to spin around with her eyes closed, as instructed by the main character who is partially visible on the right. (7) The woman in yellow continues spinning, looking slightly disoriented. The main woman watches her and laughs, holding the microphone. The background remains the same studio/indoor environment with a soft warm lamp visible on the left.

audio_base.audio_narrative_log: (1) The audio begins with a female voice speaking in a cheerful, energetic tone over a mid-tempo, upbeat pop-electronic BGM. The voice is clear with high spectral brightness. A subtle 'ding' SFX marks the beginning of the experiment explanation. (2) As the speaker demonstrates the nose-pointing task, a playful 'bubble pop' SFX sounds when her finger makes contact. The BGM maintains a consistent rhythmic pulse. (3) During the split-screen sequence, multiple voices are heard. Laughter and brief exclamations ('Wait', 'Ah') from other participants mix with the primary narration. The laughter is high-arousal and positive in valence. (4) A transition occurs with a slightly louder electronic swell in the BGM. The main speaker continues explaining the science of coordination (proprioception). Vocal intensity remains steady. (5) A sharp 'cartoon slide' SFX triggers as the challenge level increases to the spinning task. The woman in yellow can be heard laughing and gasping as she spins, her voice exhibiting slight spatial movement in the mix. (6) The video ends with a mix of conversational chatter and laughter, with the BGM fading out quickly after the final joke about driving.
